blindComparison: A stranger picks Ghost of Tsushima, and the reason is contact with the ground. In Tsushima's torii approaches every lantern, post and hall is nailed to the floor by a long raking shadow and a tight dark seam where it meets the stone. In our two establishing frames nothing does that: in `wide` I measured seven hand-verified plateau-ground boxes at y-frac 0.705 and got p50 38.7 / 43.0 / 71.9 / 76.4 / 45.7 / 48.2 / 48.9, with the only two bright ones sitting inside the lantern cluster and five of seven blue-shifted (B exceeds R by 5.5 to 12.8 code values) at magic hour -- no lit half, no shadow half, and not one cast shadow from ~15 lanterns, 3 torii, 2 pavilions or the honden. Every object therefore reads as a model standing on a printed floor. The second thing a stranger sees is that our floor has holes in it: in `hero` the box (1413,989 51x23) reads meanRGB [2.8,3.0,4.8], p50 3.1, against neighbouring flagstone (1253,989) at p50 41.3 -- 7.5% of its neighbour, hard-edged, no caster, no texture inside. The `torii` frame alone would survive the comparison on composition and vermilion; the set would not.
godRayVerdict: Both, and the honest split matters. The wash removal is a real fix and must not be reverted: the previous `sun` frame was a milky veil in which the mid-field, the sun disc and the sky chroma were all erased, and the new frame has a genuine magic-hour dome, a legible disc and restored colour. But the shadow end is over-corrected into clipping, not contrast: `sun` pixels below code 8 went 0.32% -> 12.47% and below code 4 went 0.03% -> 5.89%, `valley` went 3.53% -> 14.17% and 1.01% -> 9.20%, and the crush landed squarely on the hero foreground object -- the identical box (1772,702 228x351) on the near torii upright moved from meanRGB [128.1,73.6,40.2] p50 78.9 to [9.9,3.5,3.7] p50 3.9, i.e. a featureless black slab across ~15% of the frame width with no vermilion, no grain and no cool sky bounce. And the shafts still are not there: the reported 4-maxima/3-minima arc crosses the paper lantern, the shimenawa and both uprights (crop 0.540,0.180,0.145,0.075 shows solid geometry, and the arc's own saturation of 0.72/0.69/0.81 at its dips is vermilion lacquer, not sky), while two arcs I verified as clean sky by cropping are flat: r=130 px, 25 samples over -85deg..+85deg, p50 231.2 to 241.9, peak-to-trough 10.7; r=600 px over 135deg..195deg, p50 203.9 to 212.1, peak-to-trough 8.2. So the pass traded a wash for crushed blacks and still has not delivered the feature.
notesOnApparatus: Candidates I killed before filing, by cropping or re-probing: (1) 'the vermilion in `wide` has gone to dusty rose' -- my first probe box 0.385,0.78,0.02,0.06 read [77.9,63.0,62.5] sat 0.213, but the crop showed it straddling the gap between the two posts; the actual post at 0.3775,0.745,0.0071,0.13 reads [121.6,31.0,33.4] sat 0.715. Vermilion is fine in `wide`. (2) 'no shadow under the honden in `wide`' -- my box 0.4819,0.5222,0.0711,0.0214 turned out on crop to contain the honden's veranda, not ground; the no-shadow finding is filed on the seven verified ground boxes instead. (3) 'the leaf clusters are dark against the sun' -- my box 0.5707,0.0966,0.0197,0.0342 is ~70% sky at p50 203; the bamboo finding is therefore stated visually from the 1:1 crop 0.46,0.02,0.16,0.28 with no numeric target attached to it. (4) The opening critique's `valley` box 0.88,0.02,0.06,0.04 is called 'anti-solar' but sits roughly 34deg from the sun at (937,38) -- it is forward sky in the solar glow, so 'must be blue, saturation >= 0.22' is not a physically correct target for it; the box now reads sat 0.064 and I did not treat that as a failure. (5) The opening critique's torii sky profile at x-frac 0.70 gives zenith saturation 0.417 in this build (its own target was >= 0.38, met), but the same dome at x-frac 0.40 reads 0.496 -- the sky has strong azimuthal chroma structure that a single column misses. (6) Measurement harness: all row/arc scans import region() and stats() directly from tools/probe.mjs rather than re-decoding, so the 3-channel/4-byte-stride bug cannot occur; I cross-checked two boxes against the probe.mjs CLI (166.6 vs 167 and 243.1 vs 243) and they agree to the digit. (7) Seen but NOT filed for lack of confidence: a dashed run of bright pixels along the sunward silhouette edge of the near torii upright in `sun` (visible in crop 0.62,0.0,0.38,0.6) -- it may be a legitimate chamfer specular broken by metal fittings, and I could not separate the two at this exposure. Re-look after the crushed-shadow blocker is fixed. (8) Frames `hero`, `wide` and `torii` are essentially unchanged from the previous build (below-code-8 share 4.16->4.13%, 0.01->0.01%, 4.93->4.83%); only `sun` and `valley` moved. Verdicts on the first three are therefore judgements of a build state that this round did not touch.

findings.problem: Large hard-edged near-black patches lie on the lit flagstone plaza in the near foreground. They are amoeba/keyhole shaped, have no caster above them, have no soft penumbra, and the ground texture stops dead at their boundary. Measured on this build: box (1413,989 51x23) reads meanRGB [2.8,3.0,4.8], luma p50 3.1, p99 7.4, detail 2.53. Neighbouring flagstone of the same material 160 px away, box (1253,989 51x23), reads meanRGB [51.9,40.3,39.3], p50 41.3, detail 8.67. That is 7.5% of its neighbour in sRGB code value. A second patch right of the same lantern, box (1557,989 38x18), reads meanRGB [4.4,4.9,7.1], p50 4.0. A third and larger one sits at (1296,980 127x59): meanRGB [11.4,9.4,10.8], p50 3.6, detail 4.00, against its own left neighbour (1114,980 127x59) at p50 33.9, detail 7.95. Crop to see all three at 1:1: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-hero-r16v1.png 0.44,0.80,0.24,0.14`. CRITICAL: this is byte-identical to the previous build -- the same box on shots/phone-hero-r16.png returns p50 3.1, p99 7.4, detail 2.54. Whatever shipped this round did not touch these pixels.
findings.why: No shipped title has holes in the floor of a marketing frame. The eye reads them as missing geometry or a broken decal before it reads anything else in the lower third, and they sit directly under the shot's focal lantern. They are also darker than the scene's own ambient floor allows -- round 15 measured the fill-only plaza at p50 21.0, and these are at 3.1, so illumination is being removed below what an unlit surface under this sky can be.
findings.fix: Eliminate the near-black patches so no plaza region falls below the material's fill floor, and so the flagstone texture is visible inside the patch rather than merely lifted. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `hero`: `probe stats shots/phone-hero-rN.png 0.5581,0.8453,0.0201,0.0197` must return luma p50 >= 22 AND detail >= 5.0; `0.6150,0.8453,0.0150,0.0154` must return p50 >= 22 AND detail >= 5.0; `0.5120,0.8380,0.0500,0.0500` must return p50 >= 20 AND detail >= 6.0. GUARD against faking with a global lift: the neighbour box `0.4949,0.8453,0.0201,0.0197` must stay within 41.3 +/- 15% (35.1 to 47.5) and whole-frame p50 must stay within 74.5 +/- 8% (68.5 to 80.5). ARITHMETIC CHECK: the three target boxes total 1857 + 7493 = 9350 px = 0.32% of the 2,962,440 px frame; lifting them from p50 ~3.5 to ~24 moves the whole-frame mean by 0.32% x 20.5 = 0.07 code values and the whole-frame median not at all, so the structure target and the +/-8% frame guard are mutually satisfiable with three orders of magnitude to spare. BOX CHECK: all four boxes were cropped and looked at -- the three target boxes land inside black patches, the guard box lands on lit cobble with visible joints.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING -- DISPROVE BEFORE ACTING. Rounds 8 and 15 disproved cascade coverage, cascade weights, the caster set and PCSS for this patch, three separate times, and the standing instruction is that nobody touches cascade code for it; round 15 also proved it is not reflectance (4x darker than the darkest albedo Materials.js can produce). What is left to ablate one at a time: a local occlusion/light volume with a negative or over-ranged contribution; an occlusion term applied multiplicatively more than once along the chain; a decal or contact-darkening card stamped at the wrong intensity. Note also that this is byte-identical across the two builds -- whatever code path draws it was untouched by this round's change, which should narrow the search.

findings.problem: There are still no volumetric shafts anywhere in the two frames the contract names (ARCHITECTURE 5, non-negotiable #4: 'Volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo'). The pass delivers a smooth radial bloom halo and nothing else. Evidence, using explicit arcs of probe boxes because `detail` cannot see low-frequency structure, and using only sky regions I verified by cropping first: (a) sun disc measured at (1538,543); arc of 9x9 boxes at r=130 px, 25 samples from -85deg to +85deg, entirely inside the clean-sky window native x 1514..1710 / y 386..690 (verified by `probe crop shots/phone-sun-r16v1.png 0.598,0.330,0.080,0.260` -- pure cream gradient, no geometry): p50 236.3 237.2 237.2 237.2 238.9 237.1 233.4 231.2 232.2 235.2 237.2 238.9 238.1 239.0 238.9 238.8 239.0 241.0 241.9 241.7 239.6 238.6 237.9 237.6 237.6. Peak-to-trough 10.7 code values on a mean of 237.7, smooth and near-monotone, with no interior minimum deeper than 2.2 codes against its flanks. (b) arc of 17x17 boxes at r=600 px through the clean left sky, 120deg..200deg: the in-sky span 135deg..195deg reads 204.4 204.8 205.6 206.5 205.9 203.9 209.4 212.1 211.5 208.7 208.8 209.5 208.6 -- peak-to-trough 8.2. (c) `valley`, horizontal row of 15x15 boxes at y-frac 0.10 from x-frac 0.16 to 0.46 through backlit sky above the bamboo: 194.2 195.4 198.8 204.2 208.8 212.6 213.2 217.0 221.5 224.5 228.0 233.0 237.8 [224.7 = a bamboo culm crossing the box] 239.2 238.2 235.5 232.8 231.0 -- a single smooth rise to the sun and a smooth fall away, maximum deviation from trend ~4 codes outside the culm. (d) The angular structure reported for this build is geometry, not light: the arc at r=330 px over 55deg..115deg crosses the paper lantern, the shimenawa and both torii uprights -- `probe crop shots/phone-sun-r16v1.png 0.540,0.180,0.145,0.075` shows solid objects, and the arc's 'minima' carry saturation 0.72, 0.69, 0.81, which is vermilion lacquer.
findings.why: The single silhouette this whole setting is built around -- a low sun behind a torii and a bamboo sea -- is the reference titles' signature shot, and it is the one thing a viewer expects to see here. Without discrete shafts the backlit framings read as a lens-flare filter over a still, and the contract lists this as non-negotiable.
findings.fix: Make the pass differential: visible bars where occluders sit, nothing where they do not. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `sun`, using the verified clean-sky arc only: re-measure the sun disc centre, then sample 25 boxes of 9x9 px at r=130 px from -85deg to +85deg (this arc must stay inside native x 1514..1710, y 386..690 -- crop it and confirm before trusting it). The resulting p50 sequence must contain at least 3 interior local minima, each at least 12 code values below the mean of its two flanking local maxima. GUARD 1 against faking with gain: the 25-sample mean p50 must stay within 237.7 +/- 5% (225.8 to 249.6). GUARD 2 against faking by darkening: whole-frame `sun` p50 must stay within 105.5 +/- 8% (97.1 to 113.9) and the share of the frame below code 8 must not exceed 12.47%. ARITHMETIC CHECK: three dips of 15 codes among 25 samples lowers the arc mean by 3x15/25 = 1.8 codes = 0.76%, well inside the +/-5% guard; and the arc's 25 boxes total 2025 px = 0.07% of the frame, so nothing it does can move the whole-frame p50 guard. The two are mutually satisfiable. BOX CHECK: the r=130 annulus was cropped and confirmed to be sky with no geometry; the r=330 arc used previously was cropped and confirmed to contain the lantern, rope and uprights, which is why it is not the acceptance instrument.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 15 established the emitter is not empty (rtGodA 10.2-11.0% non-zero), that sampling is converged by N=48, that the correct direction is LESS SPREAD not more gain (raising gain is the round-7 regression that made the frame worse), and that the god-ray and mid-field-wash symptoms are one defect. This build appears to have attacked the wash half and left the spread half, since the halo is now narrower and cleaner but still angularly uniform. So the thing to measure is the pass output's angular variance at fixed radius before and after narrowing the march footprint -- not its gain, and not its sample count.

findings.problem: In the widest establishing shot the plateau -- the largest surface in the frame, the lower 55% of it -- receives no key light and nothing standing on it casts a shadow. Seven hand-verified plateau-ground boxes (60x40 px at y-frac 0.7051, each cropped and confirmed to contain only ground, chosen to avoid the fence, banners, torii and lantern bodies) read: x-frac 0.0592 meanRGB [35.9,39.1,48.7] p50 38.7; 0.1343 [43.5,43.2,50.9] p50 43.0; 0.4739 [89.8,69.6,68.8] p50 71.9; 0.5332 [94.0,75.3,74.9] p50 76.4; 0.6714 [47.8,44.3,51.3] p50 45.7; 0.8688 [49.1,48.7,57.4] p50 48.2; 0.9400 [49.2,49.1,59.2] p50 48.9. The only two warm ones sit inside the lantern cluster. The other five are all blue-shifted at magic hour (B exceeds R by 5.5 to 12.8 codes) and span only 38.7 to 48.9 -- a 10.2-code window across 2532 px of frame. Second symptom, the same defect from the other side: not one of roughly fifteen stone lanterns, three torii, two pavilions, the honden or the fence lines casts a legible shadow onto the plateau. Crop `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-wide-r16v1.png 0.42,0.78,0.16,0.20` -- each lantern sits in the centre of a bright warm disc whose brightest pixels are at the contact point: the ground ring at (1141,1084 42x16) reads p50 105.7 against open ground at (1420,1084 42x16) at p50 36.1, i.e. 2.93x brighter where the object touches, with no contact darkening at all. Crop `0.30,0.42,0.36,0.22` -- the honden, two pavilions and three torii stand on uniform pale ground with nothing under them. This is not a build-wide limit: `valley`, same build, same sun, delivers a clean 2.75x lit-to-shadow ratio on the same plaza with a correctly cool shadow -- lit (1266,913 127x35) p50 80.4 meanRGB [111.9,72.6,53.1] against fence shadow (1063,842 127x35) p50 29.2 meanRGB [27.6,32.9,41.0]. Whole-frame `wide` is also the flattest in the set: saturation 0.206, p1 18.4, and only 0.50% of pixels below code 16.
findings.why: Contact shadow is what makes a place feel real; without it everything is a model on a printed floor, which is the exact reading of this frame at thumbnail size. Worse, this is the establishing shot -- the frame a store page uses -- and it is the one that most obviously loses the blind comparison against any Tsushima vista, where the same low sun rakes across an entire field.
findings.fix: Restore a visible key and real cast shadows on the plateau in the `wide` framing. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `wide`, on the same seven verified boxes `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png <x>,0.7051,0.0237,0.0342` at x-frac 0.0592 / 0.1343 / 0.4739 / 0.5332 / 0.6714 / 0.8688 / 0.9400: (1) at least 5 of the 7 must have mean R > mean B (currently 2 of 7); (2) excluding the two lantern-cluster boxes 0.4739 and 0.5332, the remaining five must span >= 25 code values of p50 between their max and min (currently 38.7 to 48.9 = 10.2) -- some must be in sun and some in shadow; (3) at least one object shadow must be visible at 1:1 in `probe crop shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.42,0.78,0.16,0.20`, and the ground box (1141,1084 42x16) must no longer be the local maximum -- some box within 40 px of the lantern base, downsun, must read below the open-ground value 36.1. GUARD against faking with a global warm grade or exposure change: the distant-massif box `0.760,0.322,0.095,0.051` must keep p50 within 160.0 +/- 6 and the clean-sky box `0.898,0.230,0.095,0.051` must keep p50 within 153.4 +/- 8; both were cropped and confirmed to contain massif rock and sky respectively, and neither contains any plateau. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the five structure boxes total 12,000 px = 0.41% of the frame, and the two guard boxes contain zero plateau pixels, so a 25-code redistribution across the plateau cannot move either guard box at all -- the targets are trivially co-satisfiable. The whole-frame p1 is deliberately NOT guarded; it is currently 18.4 and is expected to fall as real shadows appear.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 15's bound is the thing to re-verify first: with `this.rim` counted, fill measured 0.5937 luminous irradiance against key 0.3960, so key/fill = 0.67 and the best achievable lit:shadow ratio was 1 + key/fill = 1.67x. But `valley` in THIS build measures 2.75x on the same plaza material, which is above that ceiling -- so either the ratio has changed or it is framing-dependent. Measure the current key/fill by ablation, and measure it in the `wide` pose specifically, before changing anything. DO NOT re-open cascade coverage, cascade weights, the caster set or PCSS; rounds 7, 8 and 15 disproved all four.

findings.problem: The shadow end of the two sun-facing frames has been clipped rather than deepened, and the clipping has eaten the hero foreground object. In `sun` the share of the frame below code 8 went 0.32% -> 12.47% and below code 4 went 0.03% -> 5.89% against the previous build; in `valley`, 3.53% -> 14.17% and 1.01% -> 9.20%. The near torii upright, the nearest object in `sun` and roughly 370 px / 14.6% of frame width, now reads on the identical box (1772,702 228x351): meanRGB [9.9,3.5,3.7], p50 3.9, p1 0.0, p99 24.4, detail 2.53. The same box on the previous build read [128.1,73.6,40.2], p50 78.9, p99 149.6. Crop `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-sun-r16v1.png 0.695,0.58,0.10,0.22` -- a 253x257 native crop of a lacquered vermilion post that is solid black with faint noise: no vermilion, no wood grain, no lacquer wear, and no cool sky bounce (mean B is 3.7 against R 9.9, so the shadow side is warm-neutral, not the contract's #4a6b8f). The same crush hits `valley` broadly: identical boxes fell p50 88.3 -> 65.8 (0.10,0.55), 13.1 -> 5.8 (0.30,0.88) and 66.5 -> 40.8 (0.62,0.62), with p1 falling 36.0 -> 6.3 and 16.8 -> 0.0. Note that the reported detail rise 3.11 -> 4.02 on `sun` is a contrast artefact of this crush, not new texture -- mean |Laplacian| scales with local contrast, and the same regions gained no structure.
findings.why: A backlit foreground post at magic hour should be a dark, saturated, grainy silhouette with a cool sky-lit shoulder and a hot rim, the way Sekiro's Ashina gate posts read at dusk. Ours is a die-cut black rectangle through the middle of the frame with zero information in it, which reads as a rendering failure rather than as a silhouette, and it violates ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #9 outright. Losing the ambient floor also removes the cool/warm split the whole palette is built on.
findings.fix: Restore an ambient shadow floor on the sun-facing frames without giving back the milky wash the same change correctly removed. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `sun`: `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.70,0.60,0.09,0.30` must return luma p50 between 18 and 45 inclusive, detail >= 5.0, and mean B >= 10.0. Additionally the frame's share below code 8 must fall to <= 6.0% and below code 4 to <= 2.0% (currently 12.47% and 5.89%); on `valley` the same two shares must fall to <= 8.0% and <= 4.0% (currently 14.17% and 9.20%). GUARD against giving back the wash: the clean-sky arc mean at r=130 px around the sun disc must stay within 237.7 +/- 5%, whole-frame saturation must stay >= 0.330 on `sun` (currently 0.338) and >= 0.360 on `valley` (currently 0.369), and the mid-field box `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.55,0.55,0.06,0.04` must NOT rise above p50 226 (that is the value the previous, washed build sat at). ARITHMETIC CHECK: the upright and the other crushed geometry are ~12.5% of `sun` and all of it currently sits below code 8, i.e. far below the frame median of 105.5; lifting that population to p50 ~25 leaves every one of those pixels still below the median, so the frame median does not move at all and there is no conflict with a whole-frame brightness guard -- which is why the guards above are on saturation and on a named mid-field box rather than on frame p50. BOX CHECK: 0.70,0.60,0.09,0.30 was cropped and is solid torii upright; 0.55,0.55,0.06,0.04 was checked against the crop 0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5 and contains the mid-field lantern/fence/treeline band.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Two candidates worth one ablation each: (a) whatever removed the additive atmospheric term this round removed it uniformly rather than with depth, so surfaces at 3-8 m lost the same lift as surfaces at 800 m and fell below the ambient floor; (b) a tone-curve or contrast term was steepened at the same time to compensate for the removed haze, and the two compounded at the bottom of the range. Distinguish them by measuring the same near-post box with the grade neutralised but the atmosphere change kept.

findings.problem: The sakura canopy, the largest and most eye-catching object in the hero frame, is built from large flat-shaded hard-alpha cards. At native the individual blossom clusters are 45-80 px angular polygons on a crown spanning ~700 px, each a smooth untextured facet with a hard binary alpha edge and visible stair-stepping on every boundary; the branches are drawn as flat dark strokes lying on top of the blossoms rather than passing through them. The shading is bimodal rather than continuous -- box (284,269 51x35) reads meanRGB [98.7,75.2,98.0] saturation 0.266 detail 5.91 (mauve population) while box (380,328 51x35) reads [100.4,68.8,94.0] saturation 0.325 detail 8.27, and lit cards higher in the crown run salmon [~159,84,85]: two flat colour populations with nothing in between. Crop at 1:1: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-hero-r16v1.png 0.06,0.05,0.24,0.36`.
findings.why: It is the first thing the eye lands on in the frame and it is the least finished thing in the set -- flat two-tone cutout foliage against an otherwise well-textured shrine. Tsushima's blossom trees read as thousands of small elements with translucency and light falling through them; ours reads as torn coloured paper, and no amount of quality elsewhere survives that comparison at thumbnail size.
findings.fix: Break the canopy into petal-scale elements with soft silhouette coverage and continuous shading. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `hero`: `probe stats shots/phone-hero-rN.png 0.112,0.230,0.020,0.030` must return detail >= 12.0 (currently 5.91) and `0.150,0.280,0.020,0.030` must return detail >= 12.0 (currently 8.27); no single flat-shaded facet in the crop `0.06,0.05,0.24,0.36` may exceed 25 px across at native. GUARD against faking with grain or sharpening: both boxes' meanRGB must stay within +/-8% per channel of [98.7,75.2,98.0] and [100.4,68.8,94.0], and the adjacent sky box `0.30,0.06,0.06,0.04` must keep detail below 1.0. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the two target boxes total 3570 px = 0.12% of the frame and the guard is per-box colour rather than frame-wide, so raising local high-frequency energy inside them cannot conflict with any of the guards. BOX CHECK: both boxes were cropped and land inside the shaded (mauve) part of the canopy; the sky guard box was checked to contain no blossom.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Two cheap ablations: (a) the blossom card is instanced at a world size several times larger than a real cluster, so a correct texture is simply magnified past its own detail; (b) the card material is alpha-tested with no alpha-to-coverage or dither, giving a binary silhouette at every scale, which would explain the stair-stepping independently of card size. Measure card world size and alpha mode before changing either.

findings.problem: The bamboo does not read as bamboo and does not read as backlit. The tall culms above the tree line are bare poles carrying a handful of small, detached, hard-aliased leaf clusters spaced far apart along the stem, with long empty stretches between them; every cluster boundary shows visible pixel stair-stepping against the bright sky. Crop at 1:1: `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-valley-r16v1.png 0.46,0.02,0.16,0.28`. More seriously, with the sun directly behind them the leaves show no translucency and no rim at all -- the canopy band `probe stats shots/phone-valley-r16v1.png 0.60,0.20,0.10,0.06` reads meanRGB [121.6,123.3,110.0] p50 88.1, and the tree wall at `0.08,0.20,0.06,0.08` reads [39.0,60.3,52.6] p50 54.0 saturation 0.359, i.e. dark, opaque and green-dominant against a sky at p50 200-240 immediately above it. The wall also does not lift toward the sky at all with distance: the far-left wall at p50 54.0 and the nearer right-hand wall at `0.70,0.22,0.06,0.08` p50 56.3 are within 2.3 codes of each other.
findings.why: ARCHITECTURE 9 sets SUN_AZIMUTH_DEFAULT specifically to backlight the bamboo, and it is the setting's signature: thin leaves at magic hour should glow gold-green with the sun behind them, which is exactly what sells Tsushima's bamboo strikes and Sekiro's Ashina reeds. Here they are opaque dark green cutouts, so the shot's whole reason for existing does not fire, and the sparse detached clusters read as instancing artefacts rather than plants.
findings.fix: Give the bamboo leaves transmission and give the culms continuous foliage. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `valley`: (1) the canopy band `probe stats shots/phone-valley-rN.png 0.60,0.20,0.10,0.06` must return mean R >= mean G by at least 8 code values (currently R 121.6 vs G 123.3, i.e. G leads) and saturation >= 0.32 (currently 0.247) -- backlit leaves must go warm, not stay green; (2) the tree wall `0.08,0.20,0.06,0.08` must return p50 >= 75 (currently 54.0) so it stops being an opaque black-green silhouette; (3) the isolated leaf clusters must stop being isolated: in the crop `0.46,0.02,0.16,0.28` no culm may show a bare-stem run longer than 60 px at native between clusters. GUARD against faking with a global exposure or warm grade: the clean-sky box `0.53,0.09,0.02,0.034` must keep p50 within 210.9 +/- 8 and the foreground plaza `0.55,0.78,0.12,0.12` must keep p50 within 49.8 +/- 15%. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the two target boxes total 253x70 + 152x94 = 31,998 px = 1.08% of the frame; raising them by 20 codes moves whole-frame mean by 0.22 codes, and both guard boxes are outside the canopy entirely, so the targets and guards are mutually satisfiable. BOX CHECK: 0.60,0.20,0.10,0.06 was cropped and contains canopy plus a strip of lit sky at its top (which is why the criterion is on channel ordering and saturation, not on absolute luma); 0.08,0.20,0.06,0.08 is pure tree wall; the sky guard box at 0.53,0.09 was confirmed clean by crop 0.14,0.045,0.34,0.13. NO numeric target is attached to the individual leaf clusters -- my attempt to probe one returned ~70% sky, so that half of the finding must be judged from the crop.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Candidates: (a) the leaf material has no transmission/subsurface term at all, so a thin leaf is shaded as an opaque Lambert sheet and can only ever go dark when backlit; (b) transmission exists but is being evaluated against the wrong light or clamped out at this sun elevation. Ablate by forcing a transmission term to a large value and re-measuring the same canopy box before tuning anything.

findings.problem: The shot named `valley` contains no valley. The ground runs dead flat from the foreground deck to a wall of trees at the horizon: no drop-off, no water surface anywhere in the set although ARCHITECTURE 9 puts WATER_LEVEL 30 m below the plateau, no layered receding ridges behind the tree wall, no mist, and no bamboo sea -- the bamboo is a thin fringe of spindly culms at the tree line rather than a canopy falling away below the camera. The frame therefore has three depth planes (foreground railing, flat dirt, tree wall) and no aerial-perspective ladder between them: the far-left wall reads p50 54.0 saturation 0.359 and the right-hand wall p50 56.3 saturation 0.392, i.e. distance is doing nothing to either luma or chroma. The one thing behind the tree line that could have read as depth -- the dark band at `0.02,0.37,0.10,0.03`, meanRGB [29.3,40.3,54.4] p50 38.7 -- is darker than the trees in front of it, so it recedes in the wrong direction. The mid-ground is roughly 30% of the frame and is uniform bare dirt.
findings.why: This is the only framing in the review set that is supposed to deliver the premise stated in ARCHITECTURE 5 -- 'a mountain shrine above a bamboo sea at magic hour... Mist in the valley' -- and it delivers a flat lot with a hedge at the end of it. Every Tsushima vista earns its scale from four or five stacked depth bands with haze between them; two planes cannot read as a 1.8 km view no matter how the foreground is lit.
findings.fix: The acceptance target is on the frame, whichever of the two causes it turns out to be. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `valley`: three boxes down the left third -- `probe stats shots/phone-valley-rN.png 0.10,0.72,0.06,0.03` (near), `0.10,0.55,0.06,0.03` (mid), `0.10,0.42,0.06,0.03` (far) -- must become monotone in both directions: saturation strictly falling near->far and luma p50 strictly rising near->far, with at least 20 code values of p50 between near and far and at least 0.15 of saturation between near and far. Additionally the frame must show a drop-off: some pixel column in the middle third must contain terrain surface below the foreground deck plane, i.e. `probe crop shots/phone-valley-rN.png 0.35,0.28,0.30,0.20` must show ground falling away rather than a continuous flat plain meeting the tree line. GUARD against faking with fog: the foreground plaza box `0.55,0.78,0.12,0.12` must keep saturation >= 0.28 (currently 0.320) and the sun-side sky `0.35,0.10,0.06,0.04` must keep p50 within 233.0 +/- 10. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the three profile boxes total 3x(152x35) = 15,960 px = 0.54% of the frame and the two guard boxes lie outside all three, so a 20-code / 0.15-saturation ladder across the profile cannot move either guard. BOX CHECK: all three profile boxes were cropped -- near lands on lit dirt with grass sprigs, mid on open dirt, far on the tree wall base; the sky guard box was confirmed clean of bamboo culms.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING, AND DISPROVE THIS ONE FIRST BEFORE TOUCHING THE HEIGHTFIELD. The camera may simply not be aimed over the drop, in which case the terrain is innocent and the fix is a pose change, not a reshape. Ray-march the terrain height along the `valley` view ray before concluding: if the surface stays within a few metres of PLATEAU_HEIGHT all the way to the tree line, the heightfield genuinely has no valley there; if it drops toward WATER_LEVEL just outside the frustum, report that and hand the finding back rather than reshaping anything. Round 15's SHOTS.sun result is the precedent -- a stale pose was blamed on the wrong owner for several rounds.

findings.problem: The foreground torii uprights carry no surface detail at the scale they occupy, in violation of ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #9. The right-hand upright spans native x 1726 to ~2100, the nearest object in the shot, and box (1772,702 228x351) returns detail 2.53 while the plaza in the same frame returns 5.09-6.11 and the stone lantern base returns comparable values. The centre pillar behaves the same way. There is no wood fibre, no lacquer variation, no node or joint, and no bevel highlight anywhere on either post -- only a smooth vertical gradient. NOTE: this is currently entangled with the crushed-black blocker on the same shot; the surface may exist and simply be unmeasurable at code 4. Re-measure this finding only AFTER the PostFX crushed-shadow blocker is fixed, and drop it if detail then clears 5.0 on its own.
findings.why: The largest, nearest object in a hero framing having zero surface is the classic tell of an untextured prop, and it is the one thing in the set that an art director would point at first if the exposure were correct.
findings.fix: If, after the crushed-shadow blocker is fixed, `probe stats shots/phone-sun-rN.png 0.70,0.60,0.09,0.30` still returns detail < 5.0, give the uprights real surface: vertical wood fibre, lacquer wear and node/joint breakup at a scale visible across 370 px. ACCEPTANCE: that box and `0.72,0.20,0.05,0.12` must each return detail >= 6.0. GUARD against faking with global grain or sharpening: both boxes' meanRGB must stay within +/-10% per channel of whatever the post-fix baseline is, and the clean-sky box `0.640,0.400,0.030,0.060` must keep detail below 0.6 (currently the r=130 arc region measures well under that). ARITHMETIC CHECK: the two boxes total 80,028 + 14,976 = 95,004 px = 3.2% of the frame; adding high-frequency texture inside them changes no mean value and the guards are per-box colour plus an off-post sky control, so there is no conflict. BOX CHECK: 0.70,0.60,0.09,0.30 and 0.72,0.20,0.05,0.12 were both cropped and are solid upright; the sky control at 0.640,0.400 was confirmed inside the verified clean-sky window.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Either the upright's UV scale puts the wood texture's detail band well below one pixel at this distance, or the post shares a material whose normal/roughness maps are not reaching it. Check the UV scale in metres against the 370 px on-screen width first -- that is a one-number test.

findings.problem: The dressing reads as instanced, not inhabited. In `torii` the three foreground stone lanterns are the same model at the same scale with the same texture orientation, spaced at near-equal intervals along a line, with no rotation variation, no lean, no chipped or mossy variant, and no debris around any of them. In `wide` the same lantern repeats about fifteen times in two straight rows flanking the approach at even spacing, and the three torii are the same asset at three scales along one axis. Crop `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-wide-r16v1.png 0.42,0.78,0.16,0.20` and `0.30,0.42,0.36,0.22`.
findings.why: CRITIC.md priority 8: real places have clutter, wear and asymmetry. A perfectly regular row of identical props is the single clearest signature of a level editor, and it is what makes the plateau read as a placement grid rather than a shrine that has been standing for centuries.
findings.fix: Vary the repeated dressing. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM set: in the crop `shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.42,0.78,0.16,0.20` the two visible lanterns must differ in yaw by at least 12 degrees and in height by at least 8%, and at least one of the three foreground lanterns in `shots/phone-torii-rN.png` crop `0.02,0.44,0.30,0.50` must carry a distinct surface variant (moss, chip, lichen or soot) covering at least 15% of its visible area. Additionally the along-approach spacing of the lantern row in `wide` must vary by at least 15% between consecutive gaps. GUARD: whole-frame draw calls and triangles must remain inside the ARCHITECTURE 7 budget (<= 140 draw calls, <= 900k triangles) -- variation must come from per-instance attributes, not from new draw calls. ARITHMETIC CHECK: per-instance yaw, scale and a variant index are attributes on an existing instanced draw, so the target and the draw-call guard are satisfiable simultaneously by construction; no new material or mesh is required.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. The placement pass probably emits a fixed transform per slot with no jitter and no variant channel, rather than the variation existing and being overwritten. Check whether the instance buffer carries any per-instance rotation/scale at all before adding a variant system.

findings.problem: The sky's chroma is now genuinely good but its luminance is still a plain card with no cloud form. In `torii` the vertical profile at x-frac 0.70 reads p50 146.3 / 155.2 / 165.9 at y-frac 0.02 / 0.18 / 0.36 -- a 19.6-code monotone ramp across the entire visible dome, with per-box lumaSpread 3.3 / 3.1 / 4.6 and detail 0.76 / 0.58 / 0.45. In `hero` the sky band `0.72,0.02,0.14,0.06` reads p1 165.6 to p99 173.5, a total range of 7.9 code values across a 354x70 region. There is no cumulus, no density, no shadowed cloud underside anywhere in the set -- only thin horizontal wisps in `sun` and `hero`. Correction to the record, since it changes the routing: the sky is NOT achromatic any more. `torii` zenith at x-frac 0.70 now reads meanRGB [109.5,153.4,187.7] saturation 0.417, and the same dome at x-frac 0.40 reads [92.9,140.7,184.4] saturation 0.496 with a clean monotone gradient 133.9 -> 143.4 down to the horizon. That is a real blue sky with real azimuthal structure, and it should not be re-opened as a blocker.
findings.why: Tsushima's magic-hour skies carry cloud mass with lit tops and shadowed bellies; that mass is what gives the sky depth and gives the frame a second light source to react to. A smooth ramp reads as a gradient backdrop, which is the last thing separating the `torii` frame from a store-page frame.
findings.fix: Add cloud form with density and internal shading. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `torii`: `probe stats shots/phone-torii-rN.png 0.70,0.02,0.08,0.04` and `0.70,0.18,0.08,0.04` must each return lumaSpread >= 25 (currently 3.3 and 3.1) -- i.e. there must be something in the sky that is not the gradient. On `hero`, `0.72,0.02,0.14,0.06` must return lumaSpread >= 30 (currently 7.9). GUARD against faking with noise or grain: detail in all three boxes must stay below 2.5 (cloud is low-frequency, grain is not), and the boxes' mean saturation must not fall below their current 0.417 / 0.376 / 0.210. ARITHMETIC CHECK: lumaSpread is a within-box p99-p1 measure and the saturation guard is a within-box mean, so a cloud that raises spread while keeping mean chroma satisfies both by construction; the three boxes total 28,838 px = 0.97% of a frame, so no whole-frame guard is needed. BOX CHECK: all three boxes were cropped and contain only sky -- no torii, no mountain, no roofline.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. The dome may be producing cloud density that post is then flattening -- round 15 measured that switching bloom and god rays off moved sky-adjacent saturation 0.188 -> 0.348. Sample the dome before post and check its own lumaSpread over the same solid angle before adding anything to it; if the pre-post dome already spreads > 25, hand this to PostFX rather than adding cloud.

findings.problem: A faint rectilinear lattice floats in the sky to the right of the massif -- roughly vertical hatching crossed by two or three horizontal lines, spanning about 240x60 px at native around (2274,377). It reads as a wireframe box hanging in the haze. Box `0.898,0.322,0.095,0.051` returns detail 1.14 against the clean-sky control directly above it, `0.898,0.230,0.095,0.051`, at detail 0.91, with meanRGB [162.0,159.1,162.7] and lumaSpread 18.7. The contrast is low -- the lines run about 5 to 8 code values against their surround -- but the structure is rectilinear and straight-edged, which the eye picks out of a smooth sky immediately. Crop `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-wide-r16v1.png 0.78,0.22,0.22,0.22` and look at the right half.
findings.why: Straight lines do not occur in sky. Anything rectilinear up there reads as a rendering fault -- a mesh boundary, a clipmap seam or a projection artefact -- and it is in the establishing shot.
findings.fix: Remove the rectilinear structure from the sky region. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `wide`: `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.898,0.322,0.095,0.051` must return detail <= 1.00, matching its own clean-sky control `0.898,0.230,0.095,0.051` (currently 0.91) to within 0.15, and the crop `0.78,0.22,0.22,0.22` must contain no straight line longer than 40 px at native above the mountain silhouette. GUARD against faking by blurring the sky: the control box must keep detail within 0.91 +/- 0.20 and the massif box `0.760,0.322,0.095,0.051` must keep detail within 3.02 +/- 0.60 so the far terrain is not softened along with it. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the target and both guards are three disjoint boxes totalling 43,380 px = 1.5% of the frame, and the target asks the artefact box to fall to the control box's own current value, so the two are satisfiable simultaneously by definition. BOX CHECK: all three boxes were cropped -- the target box shows the lattice, the control box is clean grey-blue sky, and the massif box is pale pink rock face.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. It sits directly above the far ridge line and is at very low contrast, which fits a distant terrain or ridge-band mesh whose backfaces or wireframe-scale geometry are showing through the haze rather than being occluded. Confirm by ablating the far-range geometry and re-shooting the same box before touching anything in the sky.
